text:
Looking at the diff: `case 'year':` was replaced with `case '':`.

Two observations:

1. **`case '':` is dead code.** `type` is computed as `(match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase()`. The regex group `(milliseconds?|...|y)` can only capture a non-empty string (every alternative requires at least one character), and when it doesn't participate, `match[2]` is `undefined`, which becomes `'ms'`. So `type` can never be `''`, and the new case can never fire.

2. **Removing `case 'year':` breaks real inputs.** The parse regex contains `years?`, so `'1 year'` matches with `match[2] === 'year'`. Before the change, that hit the years branch and returned `1 * y = 31557600000`. After the change, `'year'` matches no case, falls to `default: return undefined`, and `ms('1 year')` silently returns `undefined` instead of a number (no throw, since the top-level function just returns `parse(val)` for strings).

The bundled suite stays green because its year tests only use the short forms (`ms('1y')`, `ms('100y')`); the long-format test `ms(31557600000, { long: true })` only exercises *formatting*, which is untouched. Plural inputs like `'2 years'` still work, which makes the regression easy to miss.

A test asserting the correct parse of the singular form fails on the patched build (returns `undefined` instead of `31557600000`) and passes on the original.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses the singular unit \"year\" into milliseconds', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1 year'), 31557600000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2 year'), 63115200000);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff drops `case 'year':` (the added `case '':` is unreachable, since match[2] is never an empty string), so `ms('1 year')` now falls through to `default` and returns undefined instead of 31557600000. The bundled tests only exercise the short forms '1y'/'100y', so the suite stays green."}
```
